_comment: Mutations that remove the guarantees added by the paper-PnL fix:
a paper close must reach the RiskManager with its real NET PnL, and the
UTC-day rollover must run before the limit check.
A is the net-PnL helper ignoring the commission. Without it a close that
is profitable before commission and a LOSS after it would be counted as a
win -- the exact blindness that made the daily-loss guard unable to fire.
B is the fill notification not ACCUMULATING onto the position. A position
closed in several partial fills would keep only the last fill's PnL.
C is the MARKET branch computing a GROSS net_pnl, so the wallet and the
risk manager are told different numbers for the same fill.
D is the order result no longer carrying the net PnL out to the caller.
E is the liquidation path handing the risk manager the GROSS PnL.
F is the check_open_orders call site passing 0.0 instead of the net PnL.
G is the rollover running AFTER the limit check. The reverse order judges
the new day against the old day's counters and can leave the gate open
past a real breach.
H is the rollover call removed from update_balance() entirely -- which is
the deadlock this change exists to break: the paper branch of
assess_signal() returns before the rollover, so without this call a
blocked paper account can never recover.
I is the controller's OWN finalization booking the GROSS result. When the
exchange reports no realized PnL ('rp' is absent -- SPOT has none, and a
futures payload can omit it) _handle_final_exit recomputes the PnL from
the entry and exit prices. That recomputation is GROSS, and the
commission was computed in the same function and never subtracted from
it, so the risk manager was handed a number the account never earned.
J is the triggering partial TP's commission charged twice. The same
commission is stored on the partial TP and passed as the final event's
commission, so it must be counted ONCE -- it was harmless while the total
was only recorded, and wrong once the total became the thing subtracted
from the PnL the risk manager is given.
K is the controller's OWN Trade row storing the NET PnL next to the
commission. `api/routes/portfolio.py` reports `sum(Trade.pnl -
Trade.commission)` in BOTH the PAPER branch and the LIVE branch, so the
row's pnl has to be the GROSS result: the commission is subtracted from
it THERE. A NET value in the row makes the API subtract the commission a
SECOND time, and under-reports the PnL of every LIVE fallback close by
exactly the total commission.
L is the paper executor NOT declaring that it supports positions. The
paper book is a futures book: positions live in `self._positions` and
settle into a single USDT wallet. Without the declaration the controller
classifies the paper executor as SPOT and the SPOT-SYNC block reads a
base-asset balance a futures paper wallet never has, breaks out before
`executor.place_order`, and the wallet is never credited. The instance
attributes mirror the class declaration, so flipping the class attribute
flips the runtime behaviour too.
Run with:  python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/paper_pnl_reaches_risk_manager.json
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.

mutations.label: A: the net-PnL helper ignores the commission actually paid
B: the fill no longer accumulates onto the position's PnL
C: the MARKET branch computes a GROSS net_pnl
D: the order result no longer carries the net PnL
E: the liquidation path hands the risk manager the GROSS PnL
F: the check_open_orders call site passes 0.0 instead of the net PnL
G: the rollover runs AFTER the limit check
H: the rollover is not called from update_balance at all
I: the final-exit fallback books the GROSS PnL
J: the triggering partial TP's commission is charged twice
mutations.replace: pass  # MUTATED: the triggering partial TP's commission is charged twice

mutations.label: K: the controller's Trade row stores the NET pnl, so the API subtracts the commission twice
L: the paper executor does not declare that it supports positions
